source_name: Erste Bank Hungary LinkedIn – ErStep graduate/trainee programme communications
why_relevant: Erste Hungary announces its 'ErStep' trainee programme cohorts and business-line targets primarily via LinkedIn rather than a public careers page, making social posts the only visible signal for that pipeline. Also carries leadership-appointment posts.

source_name: Profession.hu – Hungarian job board (regional and trainee filters)
why_relevant: Largest domestic job board with city filters (Szeged, Debrecen) and employer-name search; aggregate posting counts per bank/service-centre and per city are a quantitative hiring-intensity proxy that is far more granular than press announcements.

source_name: Citi Hungary – Citi Szolgáltató Központ (Budapest Service Center) about page
why_relevant: Canonical company-side description of one of the largest foreign-bank service centres in Budapest (2,000+ staff, 25 functions). Baseline reference for measuring announced expansions (e.g. a 250-job expansion with ~HUF 250m state support on a HUF 3bn+ investment) against actual footprint.

Company-side description of Budapest as one of the firm's largest European hubs (~2,500 staff) with a named function list (technology, risk, finance, fixed income, analytics, HR, legal & compliance, internal audit) — a structural map of what a large foreign investment bank actually runs from Hungary, plus a rotational internship programme page.

Live vacancy feed for BlackRock's Budapest hub; posting volume and role mix by function are a direct, high-frequency headcount-intent signal for a major asset-manager back office in the cell's geography.

Hungarian HR trade press that covers shared-service-centre employment totals, salary and attrition trends and recruitment campaigns — the labour-market lens on the same centres, often quoting HOA data and naming employers expanding or cutting.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) – member directory and news
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of banks and foreign bank branches operating in Hungary (incl. Deutsche Bank AG Magyarországi Fióktelepe), giving exact legal names and aliases needed to query local media and company registries correctly for this cell.

SME/business magazine that covers regional job-creation stories in the Southern Great Plain (Szeged region) that fall below national-daily thresholds; useful filler for the Szeged leg where dedicated banking-SSC coverage is thin.

Dedicated ATS/career microsite of Hungary's largest home-grown payment institution (Barion Payment Zrt.). Open-role inventory over time is the cleanest proxy for headcount growth, new team formation (paytech, risk, .NET engineering) and functional build-out.

source_name: Barion – corporate site (About us / newsroom area)
why_relevant: Company-controlled page carrying leadership/company narrative and scale claims (18,000+ merchants, 500,000+ users). Baseline for who is presented as management and how the org describes itself before/after changes.

Official management roster of SimplePay Zrt., the dominant Hungarian domestic online-payment acquirer (rebranded from OTP Mobil Kft. on 1 July 2025). Highest-value single page for CxO-level change detection in HU payments.

SimplePay's own announcement stream carried the legal-form and brand change (OTP Mobil Kft. -> SimplePay Zrt.) together with the CEO appointment (Bese Péter as vezérigazgató and OTP Bank merchant-services head) — exactly the org-change + leadership-move signal class this workstream tracks.
Consumer-facing sister domain of the same issuer; duplicates and sometimes precedes corporate announcements, useful as a redundancy channel when simplepay.hu is restructured.

source_name: Revolut Hungary – Careers / Working at Revolut (HU locale)
why_relevant: Revolut is the largest foreign payments/e-money employer signal in HU (1.5m+ Hungarian users). Its HU-locale careers pages reveal whether Budapest roles are local-entity or EU-remote, and which functions (legal/regulatory, compliance) it is standing up locally.

source_name: Forbes.hu – Revolut Hungary leadership coverage (Petrás Gábor appointment)
why_relevant: Forbes.hu broke the Revolut HU country-lead appointment (Petrás Gábor, Feb 2026) and the preceding vacancy after Tamás Léder's departure, with interim cover by Eduardo Pérez Toribio. Forbes.hu is a reliable HU outlet for named fintech CxO moves and profiles.

Highest-signal HU business-finance outlet; its tag pages (fintech, barion) aggregate payment-sector org and leadership news and act as a pointer to actors not yet on the actor map. Portfolio also reliably reports deputy-CEO-level appointments in the wider sector.

Sector trade portal with a Hungarian-fintech-startup category, HUNFINTECH 20/20 rankings and FinTechShow coverage. Best single pointer for enumerating HU payment/e-money actors beyond the obvious six and for spotting founder/CxO churn in smaller PSPs.
Second HU fintech news vertical; carried the Hungarian Fintech Association presidency change. Useful redundancy and often covers association/ecosystem leadership rather than only corporate CxO moves.

source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség / Hungarian Fintech Association (HUNFINTECH)
why_relevant: Industry association (founded 2020, ~32 member firms, five-member elected board). Its member list is a ready-made actor map for HU payment/e-money fintechs, and board elections are themselves leadership-move events (e.g. Ács Zoltán elected president; Réti Bálint board member).

source_name: MNB – Pénzforgalmi intézmények supervisory data page
why_relevant: Reporting/disclosure hub for payment institutions; supports mapping which entities are active and at what scale, giving context for whether announced hiring is real expansion.

source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár – company registry profiles (Barion Payment Zrt. etc.)
why_relevant: Registry-derived company profiles list vezető tisztségviselők (officers/board members) — e.g. Boris Mihály Róbert and Kiss Sándor at Barion Payment Zrt. Officer changes appear here independent of whether the company announces them, making it the ground-truth check on PR-driven leadership claims.

source_name: OPTEN webshop – company data (Barion Payment Zrt.)
why_relevant: Second commercial registry aggregator; cross-check for officer and legal-form changes when Nemzeti Cégtár lags, and a paid route to change-notification feeds on tracked entities.

Wise's Budapest site is one of the largest payments-employer footprints in HU (historically its fastest-growing office). The office page plus its role list shows which functions (engineering, ops, customer support) are being scaled locally.

source_name: LinkedIn – HU company job pages and company feeds (Barion, Wise, Revolut)
why_relevant: Fastest-moving surface for both open roles and self-announced leadership moves in HU payments; counts of open HU roles per company are a direct hiring-intensity metric.

source_name: Prim Hírek – PayU Hungary keyword stream
why_relevant: Long-running HU tech news wire that republishes vendor press releases verbatim, including SimplePay/OTP Mobil and PayU items. Its keyword URL pattern makes per-company monitoring trivial, and it often carries releases that never reach mainstream media.

Interview-format outlet that names and profiles PSP managing directors (e.g. Váradi János, ügyvezető igazgató of PayU Magyarország, with prior Citibank/K&H background). Interviews and conference speaker lists are a reliable way to confirm who currently holds a role when no press release exists.

HR-trade outlet whose 'vezetőváltás' tag aggregates Hungarian executive changes across sectors, including financial services. Cross-sector coverage catches moves that finance media skip and provides HR-side framing (org restructuring, headcount).

Its 'karrier' section is a dedicated Hungarian appointment-announcement channel (carried the Fintech Association presidency change). Companies routinely push CxO/appointment PR here, so it catches moves that never appear in finance media.
